caption: The drawing is rendered in black and white on a beige paper background. It features a detailed illustration of a chair identified as a Hitchcock Chair (1821–1830) in the upper right, with the artist's name, Emile Gato, also noted. The chair has three horizontal back slats, with the topmost slat being the widest and slightly curved. Above the chair, there are two rectangular boxes with curved sides, each containing different decorative designs meant for the back slat of the chair. The top decorative design depicts a basket containing round fruits, flanked by floral and leafy elements. The second design is a symmetrical pattern of scrolling lines and floral motifs. The chair itself is shown in a three-quarters perspective, revealing front and side details, with minimally detailed caning on the seat and turned legs connected by horizontal supports. Fine lines are used throughout to indicate the carvings and painted details on the chair's frame and stretchers. The overall composition presents a technical and decorative study of the chair and its ornamentation.
title: Hitchcock Chair
